'''Zlil Sela''' ({{Langx|he|צליל סלע}}) is an Israeli [[mathematician]] working in the area of [[geometric group theory]]. He is a Professor of Mathematics at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. Sela is known for the solution<ref name="IP"/> of the [[Isomorphism problem for groups|isomorphism problem]] for [[torsion-free group|torsion-free]] [[word-hyperbolic group]]s and for the solution of the [[Free group|Tarski conjecture]] about equivalence of [[first-order theories]] of [[finitely generated group|finitely generated]] [[abelian group|non-abelian]] [[free group]]s.<ref name="ICM"/>

==Biographical data==
Sela received his Ph.D. in 1991 from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], where his [[doctoral advisor]] was [[Eliyahu Rips]].
Prior to his current appointment at the [[Hebrew University]], he held an Associate Professor position at [[Columbia University]] in New York.<ref name="CR">[http://www.columbia.edu/cu/record/archives/vol21/vol21_iss27/record2127.18.html Faculty Members Win Fellowships] Columbia University Record, May 15, 1996, Vol. 21, No. 27.</ref> While at Columbia, Sela won the [[Sloan Fellowship]] from the [[Sloan Foundation]].<ref name="CR"/><ref>[http://www.ams.org/notices/199607/people.pdf Sloan Fellowships Awarded] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303225244/http://www.ams.org/notices/199607/people.pdf |date=2016-03-03 }} ''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]'', vol. 43 (1996), no. 7, pp. 781–782</ref>

Sela gave an Invited Address at the 2002 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Beijing.<ref name="ICM">Z. Sela. ''Diophantine geometry over groups and the elementary theory of free and hyperbolic groups.'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. II (Beijing, 2002), pp. 87&nbsp;92, Higher Ed. Press, Beijing, 2002. {{isbn|7-04-008690-5}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ams.org/notices/200111/people.pdf Invited Speakers for ICM2002.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080906151927/http://www.ams.org/notices/200111/people.pdf |date=2008-09-06 }} [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 48, no. 11,  December 2001; pp. 1343&nbsp;1345</ref> He gave a plenary talk at the 2002 annual meeting of the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]],<ref>[http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS/Repository/1.0/Disseminate?view=body&id=pdffirstpage_1&handle=euclid.bsl/1046288726 The 2002 annual meeting of the Association for Symbolic Logic.] ''Bulletin of Symbolic Logic'', vol. 9 (2003), pp. 51–70</ref>
and he delivered an AMS Invited Address at the October 2003 meeting of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[http://www.ams.org/notices/200309/mtgs.pdf AMS Meeting at Binghamton, New York.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080518022504/http://www.ams.org/notices/200309/mtgs.pdf |date=2008-05-18 }} ''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]'', vol. 50 (2003), no. 9, p. 1174</ref> and the 2005 [[Tarski Lectures]] at the [[University of California at Berkeley]].<ref>[http://math.berkeley.edu/index.php?module=announce&ANN_user_op=view&ANN_id=37 2005 Tarski Lectures.] Department of Mathematics, [[University of California at Berkeley]]. Accessed September 14, 2008.</ref>
He was also awarded the 2003 [[Erdős Prize]] from the [[Israel Mathematical Union]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20021225073901/http://www.imu.org.il/erdos_prize.html Erdős Prize.] Israel Mathematical Union. Accessed September 14, 2008</ref>
Sela also received the 2008 [[Karp Prize|Carol Karp Prize]] from the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]] for his work on the Tarski conjecture and on discovering and developing new connections between [[model theory]] and [[geometric group theory]].<ref>[http://www.aslonline.org/Karp_recipients.html Karp Prize Recipients.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513151024/http://www.aslonline.org/Karp_recipients.html |date=2008-05-13 }} Association for Symbolic Logic. Accessed September 13, 2008</ref><ref>[http://www.ams.org/notices/200905/rtx090500637p.pdf ASL Karp and Sacks Prizes  Awarded] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141121175549/http://www.ams.org/notices/200905/rtx090500637p.pdf |date=2014-11-21 }}, ''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]'', vol. 56 (2009), no. 5, p. 638</ref>

==Mathematical contributions==
Sela's early important work was his solution<ref name="IP">Z. Sela. "The isomorphism problem for hyperbolic groups. I." ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'' (2), vol. 141 (1995), no. 2, pp. 217–283.</ref> in mid-1990s of the [[Group isomorphism problem|isomorphism problem]] for torsion-free [[word-hyperbolic group]]s. The machinery of [[group action]]s on [[real tree]]s, developed by [[Eliyahu Rips]], played a key role in Sela's approach. The solution of the isomorphism problem also relied on the notion of ''canonical representatives'' for elements of hyperbolic groups, introduced by Rips and Sela in a joint 1995 paper.<ref name="RS1">Z. Sela, and E. Rips. ''Canonical representatives and equations in hyperbolic groups'', [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] vol. 120 (1995), no. 3, pp. 489–512</ref> The machinery of the canonical representatives allowed Rips and Sela to prove<ref name="RS1"/> algorithmic solvability of finite systems of equations in torsion-free hyperbolic groups, by reducing the problem to solving equations in [[free group]]s, where the Makanin–Razborov algorithm can be applied. The technique of canonical representatives was later generalized by Dahmani<ref>François Dahmani. "Accidental parabolics and relatively hyperbolic groups."
''[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]'', vol. 153 (2006), pp. 93–127</ref> to the case of [[relatively hyperbolic group]]s and played a key role in the solution of the isomorphism problem for ''toral'' relatively hyperbolic groups.<ref>François Dahmani, and Daniel Groves, [https://doi.org/10.1007%2Fs10240-008-0014-3 "The isomorphism problem for toral relatively hyperbolic groups".] ''[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]]'', vol. 107 (2008), pp. 211–290</ref>

In his work on the isomorphism problem Sela also introduced and developed the notion of a JSJ-decomposition for word-hyperbolic groups,<ref>Z. Sela. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130203020005/http://www.springerlink.com/content/qn2dqfw0xquukbw0/?p=7370f12b59a04dc7bfb4bcaba1999688&pi=6|title="Structure and rigidity in (Gromov) hyperbolic groups and discrete groups in rank 1 Lie groups. II."}} ''[[Geometric and Functional Analysis]]'', vol. 7 (1997), no. 3, pp. 561–593</ref> motivated by the notion of a [[JSJ decomposition]] for [[3-manifold]]s. A JSJ-decomposition is a representation of a word-hyperbolic group as the [[Bass–Serre theory|fundamental group of a graph of groups]] which encodes in a canonical way all possible [[Bass–Serre theory#Splittings|splittings]] over [[infinite cyclic group|infinite cyclic]] [[subgroup]]s. The idea of JSJ-decomposition was later extended by Rips and Sela to torsion-free [[finitely presented group]]s<ref>E. Rips, and Z. Sela. "Cyclic splittings of finitely presented groups and the canonical JSJ decomposition." [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), vol. 146 (1997), no. 1, pp. 53–109</ref> and this work gave rise a systematic development of the JSJ-decomposition theory with many further extensions and generalizations by other mathematicians.<ref>M. J. Dunwoody, and M. E. Sageev. [https://doi.org/10.1007%2Fs002220050278 "JSJ-splittings for finitely presented groups over slender groups."] ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'', vol. 135 (1999), no. 1, pp. 25&nbsp;44</ref><ref>P. Scott and G. A. Swarup. [http://www.ams.org/era/2002-08-03/S1079-6762-02-00102-6/home.html "Regular neighbourhoods and canonical decompositions for groups."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090108024906/http://www.ams.org/era/2002-08-03/S1079-6762-02-00102-6/home.html |date=2009-01-08 }} ''Electronic Research Announcements of the American Mathematical Society'', vol. 8 (2002), pp. 20–28</ref><ref>B. H. Bowditch. [https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF02392898 "Cut points and canonical splittings of hyperbolic groups."] ''[[Acta Mathematica]]'', vol. 180 (1998), no. 2, pp. 145–186</ref><ref>K. Fujiwara, and P. Papasoglu, {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130203024700/http://www.springerlink.com/content/y36373n750808761/?p=3e55ed96a38d4737b6c103c1622249de&pi=2|title="JSJ-decompositions of finitely presented groups and complexes of groups."}} ''[[Geometric and Functional Analysis]]'', vol. 16 (2006), no. 1, pp. 70–125</ref> Sela applied a combination of his JSJ-decomposition and [[real tree]] techniques to prove that torsion-free word-hyperbolic groups are [[Hopfian group|Hopfian]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Sela | first = Z.
 | doi = 10.1016/S0040-9383(98)00015-9
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Topology
 | mr = 1660337
 | pages = 301–321
 | title = Endomorphisms of hyperbolic groups. I. The Hopf property
 | volume = 38
 | year = 1999| doi-access = free
 }}</ref> This result and Sela's approach were later generalized by others to [[finitely generated group|finitely generated]] [[subgroup]]s of hyperbolic groups<ref>Inna Bumagina, [https://doi.org/10.1023%2FB%3AGEOM.0000033859.35966.4a "The Hopf property for subgroups of hyperbolic groups."] ''[[Geometriae Dedicata]]'', vol. 106 (2004), pp. 211–230</ref> and to the setting of relatively hyperbolic groups.

Sela's most important work came in early 2000s when he produced a solution to a famous [[Free group#Tarski's problems|Tarski conjecture]]. Namely, in a long series of papers,<ref>Z. Sela. [https://doi.org/10.1007%2Fs10240-001-8188-y "Diophantine geometry over groups. I. Makanin-Razborov diagrams."] ''Publications Mathématiques''. Institut de Hautes Études Scientifiques, vol. 93 (2001), pp. 31–105</ref><ref>Z. Sela. [https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF02787407 ''Diophantine geometry over groups. II. Completions, closures and formal solutions.''] ''Israel Journal of Mathematics'', vol. 134 (2003), pp. 173–254</ref><ref>Z. Sela. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130203064508/http://www.springerlink.com/content/w8288nx4786ku012/?p=56da1a89f89046429316cc73528221a8&pi=0|title="Diophantine geometry over groups. III. Rigid and solid solutions."}} ''Israel Journal of Mathematics'', vol. 147 (2005), pp. 1–73</ref><ref>Z. Sela. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130203005151/http://www.springerlink.com/content/n6865q5628j84361/?p=e429e20ea2f14b20915ef14c533fa0c1&pi=0|title="Diophantine geometry over groups. IV. An iterative procedure for validation of a sentence."}} ''Israel Journal of Mathematics'', vol. 143 (2004), pp. 1–130</ref><ref>Z. Sela. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130203200836/http://www.springerlink.com/content/r162825432212217/?p=93a1c03b293b41ef8cb8c6136b47c083&pi=0|title="Diophantine geometry over groups. V<sub>1</sub>. Quantifier elimination. I."}} ''Israel Journal of Mathematics'', vol. 150 (2005), pp. 1–197</ref><ref>Z. Sela. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130203010756/http://www.springerlink.com/content/w076142801040u05/?p=2d33d0052c1749aeb7b127871d580675&pi=1|title="Diophantine geometry over groups. V<sub>2</sub>. Quantifier elimination. II."}} ''[[Geometric and Functional Analysis]]'', vol. 16 (2006), no. 3, pp. 537–706</ref><ref>Z. Sela. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130202223434/http://www.springerlink.com/content/r53x383mj14206v1/?p=2d33d0052c1749aeb7b127871d580675&pi=2|title="Diophantine geometry over groups. VI. The elementary theory of a free group."}} ''[[Geometric and Functional Analysis]]'', vol. 16 (2006), no. 3, pp. 707–730</ref> he proved that any two non-abelian [[finitely generated group|finitely generated]] [[free group]]s have the same [[first-order theory]]. His work relied on applying his earlier JSJ-decomposition and [[real tree]] techniques as well as developing new ideas and machinery of "[[algebraic geometry]]" over free groups.

Sela pushed this work further to study first-order theory of arbitrary torsion-free word-hyperbolic groups and to characterize all groups that are elementarily equivalent to (that is, have the same first-order theory as) a given torsion-free word-hyperbolic group. In particular, his work implies that if a finitely generated group ''G'' is elementarily equivalent to a word-hyperbolic group then ''G'' is word-hyperbolic as well.

Sela also proved that the first-order theory of a finitely generated free group is [[Stable theory|stable]] in the model-theoretic sense, providing a brand-new and qualitatively different source of examples for the stability theory.

An alternative solution for the Tarski conjecture has been presented by [[Olga Kharlampovich]] and [[Alexei Myasnikov]].<ref>O. Kharlampovich, and A. Myasnikov. [http://www.ams.org/era/1998-04-14/S1079-6762-98-00047-X/home.html "Tarski's problem about the elementary theory of free groups has a positive solution."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907015307/http://www.ams.org/era/1998-04-14/S1079-6762-98-00047-X/home.html |date=2008-09-07 }} ''Electronic Research Announcements of the American Mathematical Society'', vol. 4 (1998), pp. 101–108</ref><ref>O. Kharlampovich, and A. Myasnikov. ''Implicit function theorem over free groups.'' Journal of Algebra, vol. 290 (2005), no. 1, pp. 1–203</ref><ref>O. Kharlampovich, and A. Myasnikov. "Algebraic geometry over free groups: lifting solutions into generic points." ''Groups, languages, algorithms'', pp. 213–318, Contemporary Mathematics, vol. 378, [[American Mathematical Society]], Providence, RI, 2005</ref><ref>O. Kharlampovich, and A. Myasnikov. "Elementary theory of free non-abelian groups." ''Journal of Algebra'', vol. 302 (2006), no. 2, pp. 451–552</ref>

The work of Sela on first-order theory of free and word-hyperbolic groups substantially influenced the development of [[geometric group theory]], in particular by stimulating the development and the study of the notion of [[limit group]]s and of [[relatively hyperbolic group]]s.<ref>Frédéric Paulin.
''Sur la théorie élémentaire des groupes libres (d'après Sela).'' Astérisque No. 294 (2004), pp. 63–402</ref>

==Sela's classification theorem==
Theorem. Two non-abelian torsion-free hyperbolic groups are elementarily equivalent [[if and only if]] their cores are isomorphic.<ref>{{cite arXiv|year=2020|title=Towers and the first-order theory of hyperbolic groups|author=Guirardel, Vincent|author2=Levitt, Gilbert|author3=Salinos, Rizos|class=math.GR |eprint=2007.14148 }} (See p. 8.)</ref>
